name: TCA9554PWR
title: TCA9554: 8-bit I2C/SMBus I/O expander with interrupt output, 1.65 V to 5.5 V
summary: The TCA9554 gives a two-wire I2C or SMBus host eight extra general-purpose I/O lines, P0 to P7. Each line is set as input or output by a configuration register; outputs are latched push-pull stages strong enough to sink LED current, and inputs have a 100 kΩ (typ) pull-up to VCC. An open-drain, active-low INT output tells the host when an input has changed. Three address pins give eight addresses (0x20 to 0x27); the supply runs from 1.65 V to 5.5 V and the bus to 400 kHz. It comes in 16-pin TSSOP (PW), SSOP (DB, DBQ) and SOIC (DW) packages.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A host controller drives the expander over SDA and SCL and watches its INT line; each of the three lines has a 10 kΩ pull-up to the same VCC that feeds the expander. A2, A1 and A0 are grounded, so the address is 0100000. P0, P2 and P3 are outputs: P0 sinks an LED fed from VCC through 2 kΩ, P2 drives the RESET input of a second subsystem (a counter), and P3 drives the ENABLE input of a bus switch (a CBT device) joining two outside nodes A and B. P1, P4 and P5 are inputs: P1 reads the INT output of a first subsystem (a temperature sensor), P4 reads the ALARM output of a third subsystem, and P5 reads a push-button that connects it through a resistor to VCC. P6 and P7 are unused and held by their internal 100 kΩ pull-ups.

circuits.title: LED on a port with a high-value resistor in parallel
circuits.description: An LED and its series resistor hang from VCC to a port pin, and a 100 kΩ resistor runs from VCC straight to the same pin, across the LED and its resistor. With the LED dark and the port reading, the 100 kΩ holds the pin at VCC instead of one LED threshold below it, so the input does not draw extra supply current.

circuits.title: LED on a port with the expander on a lower supply
circuits.description: The expander runs from 3.3 V while its LED and series resistor are fed from 5 V into a port pin. With VCC lower than the LED supply by at least the LED threshold, the pin sits at or above VCC while the port reads and the LED is dark, so no extra supply current flows.

operation.text: Four 8-bit registers do the work: Input Port, Output Port, Polarity Inversion and Configuration. Every port is an input after power-up; the host turns any of them into outputs through the Configuration register. All four registers can be read back. The output stages are latched and can drive LEDs directly. The TCA9554A is the same device with a different fixed address, so eight of each (sixteen in all) can share a bus. The TCA9534 is the same device without the internal port pull-ups.

As an input, both output transistors are off and the pin is high impedance apart from a 100 kΩ (typ) pull-up to VCC. An input may be driven up to 5.5 V even above VCC, but current then flows from the pin through the pull-up into VCC. As an output, either the high-side or the low-side transistor is on, according to the Output Port register, giving a low-impedance path to VCC or GND; outside voltages on the pin must then stay within the recommended levels. Each port has an ESD diode to GND.

INT goes low, within tiv, on any rising or falling edge at a port set as an input. It clears when the inputs return to the state last captured or when the Input Port register is read; on a read it clears at the acknowledge bit, after the rising SCL edge. A change arriving during that acknowledge clock may be missed or show only as a brief pulse. Bus traffic to other devices does not touch the interrupt, and a port set as an output never raises it. Turning an output into an input can give a false interrupt if the pin level differs from the Input Port register. INT is open drain and needs a pull-up to VCC.

From 0 V, an internal reset holds the device until VCC reaches VPORR (1.2 V typ, 1.5 V max); then the registers and the bus state machine take their defaults. To reset it again, VCC must go below VPORF (0.75 V min, 1 V typ) and come back up. A complete reset takes a power cycle; the host can use one to recover from a bus timeout or other faulty operation. The supply ramps, re-ramp delay and glitch limits that give a clean reset are in the supply sequencing table; bypass capacitance, source impedance and the device's own impedance all affect how a glitch is seen.

SCL and SDA both need pull-up resistors to a positive supply. A transfer begins with a Start (SDA falling while SCL is high) and ends with a Stop (SDA rising while SCL is high), both sent by the master; SDA must hold steady while SCL is high at all other times. Bytes go MSB first, each followed by an acknowledge bit pulled low by the receiver; the master ends a read by leaving the last byte unacknowledged. The address pins must not change between Start and Stop. SCL and SDA inputs have noise filters.
The 7-bit address is 0100, then A2, A1, A0, giving 0x20 to 0x27 (32 to 39 decimal). The bit after the address is R/W: 1 reads, 0 writes.

After the address, a write carries a command byte whose two lowest bits select Input Port (0x00), Output Port (0x01), Polarity Inversion (0x02) or Configuration (0x03). The command byte is only sent in a write; reads keep returning the selected register until a new command byte arrives, and it never increments by itself. Input Port shows the logic level on every pin, inputs and outputs alike, and ignores writes. Output Port sets the level of pins configured as outputs; reading it returns the flip-flop contents, not the pin. A 1 in Polarity Inversion inverts the reading of that input; 0 keeps it as is. A 1 in Configuration makes the pin an input with its driver off; 0 makes it an output.

Start, address with R/W = 0, command byte, then data. Several data bytes in one write all go to the same register, so the last one stays. A Stop ends it. Output pins change within tpv after the acknowledge of the data byte.

Write the address with R/W = 0 and the command byte, send a repeated Start, then the address with R/W = 1; the device sends the selected register. Any number of bytes can follow, all from that same register; the master leaves the last one unacknowledged. Input data is taken at the rising edge of the acknowledge clock. A transfer can be cut short by a Stop at any point.

operation.topic: Supply current with LEDs on ports
operation.text: ICC rises as the voltage on a port set as an input falls below VCC. An LED from VCC through a resistor leaves the pin one LED threshold below VCC when the LED is off and the port is an input. Two ways to keep the pin at or above VCC: a high-value resistor across the LED, or running the expander from a supply lower than the LED supply by at least the LED threshold. No outside pull-up is needed on the ports.

operation.topic: Pull-up resistors on SCL and SDA
operation.text: The lowest usable pull-up is set by VCC, the highest allowed low level and the sink current; the highest is set by the allowed rise time and the bus capacitance. In Fast-mode the rise time is 300 ns.

I2C speeds need no impedance matching or differential pairs. Keep bypass and decoupling capacitors on VCC as close to the device as possible: a larger one for short supply dips and a smaller one for high-frequency ripple. Two layers can work, signals on top and a split VCC/GND plane underneath; four layers, with inner ground and power planes, suit denser routing. Vias to the planes sit right beside the VCC and GND pads. Avoid right-angle traces, spread traces apart as they leave the chip, and use wider traces for power and ground.
